chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), in [the matter of]

If a man frees his slave-girl and says to her, 'Your manumission is your dowry,' and then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, he said: 'Half of her returns to being a slave, and he has the option to keep her as a slave for the other half.'

key_terms.يَدخُلَ بِهَا: he consummates the marriage with her
key_terms.يَستَسعِيهَا: he has the option/choice regarding her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man frees his slave-girl as her dowry and divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar illustrates the concept of partial manumission (itq nisf) within Shia jurisprudence, where the slave-girl's status is split into two halves upon divorce prior to consummation. The master retains the right to either keep her as a slave for the remaining half-value or pay the equivalent to secure her full freedom, highlighting the intersection of marriage contracts and property rights in classical fiqh.
